sanskrit: na te vegaṃ viṣahituṃ śaktās tava viśāṃ pate asmābhir abhiguptasya tasmād uttiṣṭha bhārata
english: They will not be able to withstand your onslaught, O lord of peoples, when you are shielded by us. Therefore rise, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca diṣṭyā paśyāmi vo muktān īdṛśāt puruṣakṣayāt pāṇḍukauravasaṃmardāj jīvamānān nararṣabhān
english: Duryodhana said: By good fortune I see you delivered from such a slaughter of men, surviving still, O bulls among men, from the deadly clash of Pāṇḍava and Kaurava.

sanskrit: vijeṣyāmo vayaṃ sarve viśrāntā vigataklamāḥ bhavantaś ca pariśrāntā vayaṃ ca bhṛśavikṣatāḥ udīrṇaṃ ca balaṃ teṣāṃ tena yuddhaṃ na rocaye
english: We shall conquer them all once we are rested and our weariness has passed. But you are exhausted, and I am gravely wounded, while their force is at its height; for that reason I do not favor battle now.

sanskrit: na tv etad adbhutaṃ vīrā yad vo mahad idaṃ manaḥ asmāsu ca parā bhaktir na tu kālaḥ parākrame
english: It is no marvel, O heroes, that your spirit is so great and your devotion to us so supreme; yet this is not the hour for valor.

sanskrit: viśramyaikāṃ niśām adya bhavadbhiḥ sahito raṇe pratiyotsyāmy ahaṃ śatrūñ śvo na me 'sty atra saṃśayaḥ
english: Having rested this one night, I shall tomorrow give battle to the enemy at your side; of this I have no doubt.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evam ukto 'bravīd drauṇī rājānaṃ yuddhadurmadam uttiṣṭha rājan bhadraṃ te vijeṣyāmo raṇe parān
english: Saṃjaya said: Thus addressed, the son of Droṇa spoke to the king, frenzied for battle: Rise, O king—good fortune to you—we shall conquer the foe in war.

sanskrit: iṣṭāpūrtena dānena satyena ca japena ca śape rājan yathā hy adya nihaniṣyāmi somakān
english: By my sacrifices and pious works, by charity, by truth, and by my prayers I swear, O king, that this very day I shall slay the Somakas.

sanskrit: mā sma yajñakṛtāṃ prītiṃ prāpnuyāṃ sajjanocitām yadīmāṃ rajanīṃ vyuṣṭāṃ na nihanmi parān raṇe
english: May I never attain the joy fitting for the virtuous that belongs to those who have performed sacrifices, if, when this night has passed, I do not slay the enemy in battle.

sanskrit: nāhatvā sarvapāñcālān vimokṣye kavacaṃ vibho iti satyaṃ bravīmy etat tan me śṛṇu janādhipa
english: Until I have slain all the Pāñcālas I shall not loosen my armor, O lord; this I declare as truth—hear it from me, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: teṣu saṃbhāṣamāṇeṣu vyādhās taṃ deśam āyayuḥ māṃsabhārapariśrāntāḥ pānīyārthaṃ yadṛcchayā
english: While they were thus conversing, certain hunters came by chance to that place, weary beneath their loads of meat, seeking water.

sanskrit: te hi nityaṃ mahārāja bhīmasenasya lubdhakāḥ māṃsabhārān upājahrur bhaktyā paramayā vibho
english: For these hunters, O great king, were ever in Bhīmasena's service, bringing him their loads of meat with the deepest devotion, O lord.

sanskrit: te tatra viṣṭhitās teṣāṃ sarvaṃ tad vacanaṃ rahaḥ duryodhanavacaś caiva śuśruvuḥ saṃgatā mithaḥ
english: Halting there, gathered together among themselves, they overheard in secret all that the warriors said, and Duryodhana's words as well.

sanskrit: te 'pi sarve maheṣvāsā ayuddhārthini kaurave nirbandhaṃ paramaṃ cakrus tadā vai yuddhakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: And all those mighty bowmen, longing for battle, pressed the Kaurava with the utmost insistence, though he had no wish to fight.

sanskrit: tāṃs tathā samudīkṣyātha kauravāṇāṃ mahārathān ayuddhamanasaṃ caiva rājānaṃ sthitam ambhasi
english: Watching thus those great chariot-warriors of the Kauravas, and the king who lingered in the waters with no mind for battle—

sanskrit: teṣāṃ śrutvā ca saṃvādaṃ rājñaś ca salile sataḥ vyādhābhyajānan rājendra salilasthaṃ suyodhanam
english: having heard their conversation and the words of the king who lay within the water, the hunters came to know, O lord of kings, that Suyodhana was hidden in the lake.

sanskrit: te pūrvaṃ pāṇḍuputreṇa pṛṣṭā hy āsan sutaṃ tava yadṛcchopagatās tatra rājānaṃ parimārgitāḥ
english: These men had earlier been questioned by the son of Pāṇḍu about your son; coming there by chance, they had been seeking the king.

sanskrit: tatas te pāṇḍuputrasya smṛtvā tad bhāṣitaṃ tadā anyonyam abruvan rājan mṛgavyādhāḥ śanair idam
english: Then, recalling what the son of Pāṇḍu had said, the deer-hunters spoke softly to one another, O king, in this wise:

sanskrit: duryodhanaṃ khyāpayāmo dhanaṃ dāsyati pāṇḍavaḥ suvyaktam iti naḥ khyāto hrade duryodhano nṛpaḥ
english: "Let us reveal Duryodhana; the Pāṇḍava will give us wealth. Plainly enough, King Duryodhana has been disclosed to us in the lake."

sanskrit: tasmād gacchāmahe sarve yatra rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ ākhyātuṃ salile suptaṃ duryodhanam amarṣaṇam
english: "Therefore let us all go to where King Yudhiṣṭhira is, to tell him that the wrathful Duryodhana lies asleep in the water."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭrātmajaṃ tasmai bhīmasenāya dhīmate śayānaṃ salile sarve kathayāmo dhanurbhṛte
english: "Let us all tell the wise Bhīmasena, the wielder of the bow, that the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra lies hidden in the water."

sanskrit: sa no dāsyati suprīto dhanāni bahulāny uta kiṃ no māṃsena śuṣkeṇa parikliṣṭena śoṣiṇā
english: "Well pleased, he will give us abundant riches. What use to us is this dry, withered, shriveled meat?"

sanskrit: evam uktvā tato vyādhāḥ saṃprahṛṣṭā dhanārthinaḥ māṃsabhārān upādāya prayayuḥ śibiraṃ prati
english: Having spoken thus, the hunters, greatly delighted and eager for wealth, took up their loads of meat and set out toward the camp.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāś ca mahārāja labdhalakṣāḥ prahāriṇaḥ apaśyamānāḥ samare duryodhanam avasthitam
english: And the Pāṇḍavas, O great king, sure-aimed and hard-striking warriors, not seeing Duryodhana standing on the field of battle,

sanskrit: nikṛtes tasya pāpasya te pāraṃ gamanepsavaḥ cārān saṃpreṣayām āsuḥ samantāt tad raṇājiram
english: and longing to reach the end of that wicked deceiver's trickery, sent out scouts in every direction across the field of war.

sanskrit: āgamya tu tataḥ sarve naṣṭaṃ duryodhanaṃ nṛpam nyavedayanta sahitā dharmarājasya sainikāḥ
english: Returning, all the soldiers together reported to the Dharma-king that King Duryodhana had vanished.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā cārāṇāṃ bharatarṣabha cintām abhyagamat tīvrāṃ niśaśvāsa ca pārthivaḥ
english: Hearing those words of the scouts, O bull of the Bhāratas, the king fell into bitter brooding and drew a heavy sigh.

sanskrit: atha sthitānāṃ pāṇḍūnāṃ dīnānāṃ bharatarṣabha tasmād deśād apakramya tvaritā lubdhakā vibho
english: Then, O bull of the Bhāratas, while the Pāṇḍavas stood there dejected, the hunters, hastening away from that place, O lord,

sanskrit: ājagmuḥ śibiraṃ hṛṣṭā dṛṣṭvā duryodhanaṃ nṛpam vāryamāṇāḥ praviṣṭāś ca bhīmasenasya paśyataḥ
english: came joyfully to the camp, having seen King Duryodhana; and though held back, they pressed in within sight of Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: te tu pāṇḍavam āsādya bhīmasenaṃ mahābalam tasmai tat sarvam ācakhyur yad vṛttaṃ yac ca vai śrutam
english: Coming before the Pāṇḍava Bhīmasena of mighty strength, they told him all that had happened and all that they had heard.

sanskrit: tato vṛkodaro rājan dattvā teṣāṃ dhanaṃ bahu dharmarājāya tat sarvam ācacakṣe paraṃtapaḥ
english: Then Vṛkodara, O king, the scorcher of foes, having given them abundant wealth, related the whole matter to the Dharma-king.

sanskrit: asau duryodhano rājan vijñāto mama lubdhakaiḥ saṃstabhya salilaṃ śete yasyārthe paritapyase
english: "That Duryodhana, O king, has been discovered for me by the hunters; he for whose sake you grieve lies asleep, having stilled the waters about him."

sanskrit: tad vaco bhīmasenasya priyaṃ śrutvā viśāṃ pate ajātaśatruḥ kaunteyo hṛṣṭo 'bhūt saha sodaraiḥ
english: Hearing those welcome words of Bhīmasena, O lord of peoples, Ajātaśatru, the son of Kuntī, rejoiced together with his brothers.

sanskrit: taṃ ca śrutvā maheṣvāsaṃ praviṣṭaṃ salilahradam kṣipram eva tato 'gacchat puraskṛtya janārdanam
english: And learning that the great bowman had entered the watery lake, he set out at once, placing Janārdana at the fore.

sanskrit: tataḥ kilakilāśabdaḥ prādurāsīd viśāṃ pate pāṇḍavānāṃ prahṛṣṭānāṃ pāñcālānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Then there arose a tumult of glad shouting, O lord of peoples, from the exultant Pāṇḍavas and Pāñcālas on every side.

sanskrit: siṃhanādāṃs tataś cakruḥ kṣveḍāṃś ca bharatarṣabha tvaritāḥ kṣatriyā rājañ jagmur dvaipāyanaṃ hradam
english: They raised lion-roars and battle-cries, O bull of the Bhāratas; and the warriors hastened, O king, to the lake of Dvaipāyana.

sanskrit: jñātaḥ pāpo dhārtarāṣṭro dṛṣṭaś cety asakṛd raṇe prākrośan somakās tatra hṛṣṭarūpāḥ samantataḥ
english: "The wicked son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra is found, he is seen!"—again and again in the fray the Somakas cried out there on all sides, their faces glad.

sanskrit: teṣām āśu prayātānāṃ rathānāṃ tatra veginām babhūva tumulaḥ śabdo divaspṛk pṛthivīpate
english: From their swift-moving, speeding chariots there arose a tumultuous din that touched the heavens, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: duryodhanaṃ parīpsantas tatra tatra yudhiṣṭhiram anvayus tvaritās te vai rājānaṃ śrāntavāhanāḥ
english: Eager to lay hold of Duryodhana, they followed King Yudhiṣṭhira here and there in haste, their mounts worn out.

sanskrit: arjuno bhīmasenaś ca mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pāñcālyaḥ śikhaṇḍī cāparājitaḥ
english: Arjuna and Bhīmasena, and the two Pāṇḍava sons of Mādrī, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna the Pāñcāla, and the unvanquished Śikhaṇḍin,

sanskrit: uttamaujā yudhāmanyuḥ sātyakiś cāparājitaḥ pāñcālānāṃ ca ye śiṣṭā draupadeyāś ca bhārata hayāś ca sarve nāgāś ca śataśaś ca padātayaḥ
english: Uttamaujas, Yudhāmanyu, and the unconquered Sātyaki, and those Pāñcālas who remained, and the sons of Draupadī, O Bhārata, and all the horses and elephants, and foot-soldiers by the hundred—

sanskrit: tataḥ prāpto mahārāja dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ dvaipāyanahradaṃ khyātaṃ yatra duryodhano 'bhavat
english: then, O great king, the son of Dharma, Yudhiṣṭhira, reached the famed lake of Dvaipāyana, where Duryodhana was.

sanskrit: śītāmalajalaṃ hṛdyaṃ dvitīyam iva sāgaram māyayā salilaṃ stabhya yatrābhūt te sutaḥ sthitaḥ
english: Its waters cool and clear and pleasing, like a second ocean—there your son had taken his stand, having stilled the waters by his magic.

sanskrit: atyadbhutena vidhinā daivayogena bhārata salilāntargataḥ śete durdarśaḥ kasya cit prabho mānuṣasya manuṣyendra gadāhasto janādhipaḥ
english: By a most wondrous device, through the working of fate, O Bhārata, he lay sunk within the water, hard for any man to behold, O lord—the ruler of men, club in hand, O sovereign of men.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā salitāntargato vasan śuśruve tumulaṃ śabdaṃ jaladopamaniḥsvanam
english: Then King Duryodhana, dwelling sunk within the water, heard the tumultuous din, loud as a thundercloud's roar.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiras tu rājendra hradaṃ taṃ saha sodaraiḥ ājagāma mahārāja tava putravadhāya vai
english: And Yudhiṣṭhira, O lord of kings, came to that lake with his brothers, O great king, to slay your son.

sanskrit: mahatā śaṅkhanādena rathanemisvanena ca uddhunvaṃś ca mahāreṇuṃ kampayaṃś cāpi medinīm
english: With the great blast of conch-shells and the rumble of chariot-wheels, raising up a vast cloud of dust and making the earth tremble,

sanskrit: yaudhiṣṭhirasya sainyasya śrutvā śabdaṃ mahārathāḥ kṛtavarmā kṛpo drauṇī rājānam idam abruvan
english: the great chariot-warriors Kṛtavarman, Kṛpa, and the son of Droṇa, hearing the din of Yudhiṣṭhira's army, spoke thus to the king:

sanskrit: ime hy āyānti saṃhṛṣṭāḥ pāṇḍavā jitakāśinaḥ apayāsyāmahe tāvad anujānātu no bhavān
english: "Here come the Pāṇḍavas, exultant and flushed with victory. We shall withdraw for now—give us leave, O lord."

sanskrit: duryodhanas tu tac chrutvā teṣāṃ tatra yaśasvinām tathety uktvā hradaṃ taṃ vai māyayāstambhayat prabho
english: Duryodhana, hearing this from those glorious men, said "So be it," and by his magic stilled that lake, O lord.

sanskrit: te tv anujñāpya rājānaṃ bhṛśaṃ śokaparāyaṇāḥ jagmur dūraṃ mahārāja kṛpaprabhṛtayo rathāḥ
english: Having taken leave of the king, deeply sunk in grief, those chariot-warriors led by Kṛpa went far off, O great king.

sanskrit: te gatvā dūram adhvānaṃ nyagrodhaṃ prekṣya māriṣa nyaviśanta bhṛśaṃ śrāntāś cintayanto nṛpaṃ prati
english: Having traveled a long way, they spied a banyan tree, O venerable one, and sat down, sorely wearied, brooding upon the king.

sanskrit: viṣṭabhya salilaṃ supto dhārtarāṣṭro mahābalaḥ pāṇḍavāś cāpi saṃprāptās taṃ deśaṃ yuddham īpsavaḥ
english: The mighty son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra slept, having stilled the water; and the Pāṇḍavas too had reached that place, eager for battle.

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu yuddhaṃ bhavitā kathaṃ rājā bhaviṣyati kathaṃ nu pāṇḍavā rājan pratipatsyanti kauravam
english: "How then will the battle come about? What will become of the king? How, O king, will the Pāṇḍavas deal with the Kaurava?"

sanskrit: ity evaṃ cintayantas te rathebhyo 'śvān vimucya ha tatrāsāṃ cakrire rājan kṛpaprabhṛtayo rathāḥ
english: Brooding thus, those chariot-warriors led by Kṛpa unyoked their horses from the chariots and took their rest there, O king.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tatas teṣv apayāteṣu ratheṣu triṣu pāṇḍavāḥ taṃ hradaṃ pratyapadyanta yatra duryodhano 'bhavat
english: Saṃjaya said: Then, when those three chariot-warriors had departed, the Pāṇḍavas drew near to the lake where Duryodhana was.

sanskrit: āsādya ca kuruśreṣṭha tadā dvaipāyanahradam stambhitaṃ dhārtarāṣṭreṇa dṛṣṭvā taṃ salilāśayam vāsudevam idaṃ vākyam abravīt kurunandanaḥ
english: Reaching the lake of Dvaipāyana, O best of the Kurus, and seeing that body of water held fast by the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the delight of the Kurus spoke these words to Vāsudeva:

sanskrit: paśyemāṃ dhārtarāṣṭreṇa māyām apsu prayojitām viṣṭabhya salilaṃ śete nāsya mānuṣato bhayam
english: "Behold this magic the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra has worked upon the waters! Having stilled the water, he lies there; he has no fear of any man."

sanskrit: daivīṃ māyām imāṃ kṛtvā salilāntargato hy ayam nikṛtyā nikṛtiprajño na me jīvan vimokṣyate
english: "Having wrought this divine illusion, he has sunk himself within the water; yet that knower of trickery shall not escape me alive through his deceit."

sanskrit: yady asya samare sāhyaṃ kurute vajrabhṛt svayam tathāpy enaṃ hataṃ yuddhe loko drakṣyati mādhava
english: "Even if the wielder of the thunderbolt himself should lend him aid in battle, still the world shall see him slain in war, O Mādhava."

sanskrit: śrīvāsudeva uvāca māyāvina imāṃ māyāṃ māyayā jahi bhārata māyāvī māyayā vadhyaḥ satyam etad yudhiṣṭhira
english: The illustrious Vāsudeva said: Destroy this illusion of the illusionist by illusion, O Bhārata. The trickster must be slain by trickery—this is the truth, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: kriyābhyupāyair bahulair māyām apsu prayojya ha jahi tvaṃ bharataśreṣṭha pāpātmānaṃ suyodhanam
english: By many ways and means working an illusion upon the waters, slay the wicked-souled Suyodhana, O best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: kriyābhyupāyair indreṇa nihatā daityadānavāḥ kriyābhyupāyair bahubhir balir baddho mahātmanā
english: By ways and means Indra slew the Daityas and Dānavas; by manifold ways and means the great-souled one bound Bali.

sanskrit: kriyābhyupāyaiḥ pūrvaṃ hi hiraṇyākṣo mahāsuraḥ hiraṇyakaśipuś caiva kriyayaiva niṣūditau vṛtraś ca nihato rājan kriyayaiva na saṃśayaḥ
english: By ways and means of old the great Asura Hiraṇyākṣa, and Hiraṇyakaśipu too, were destroyed by stratagem; and Vṛtra was slain, O king, by stratagem alone—of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: tathā paulastyatanayo rāvaṇo nāma rākṣasaḥ rāmeṇa nihato rājan sānubandhaḥ sahānugaḥ kriyayā yogam āsthāya tathā tvam api vikrama
english: So too the rākṣasa named Rāvaṇa, son of Pulastya's line, was slain by Rāma, O king, together with his kin and his followers, through resort to a contrived design; therefore do you also show your prowess thus.

sanskrit: kriyābhyupāyair nihato mayā rājan purātane tārakaś ca mahādaityo vipracittiś ca vīryavān
english: By ways and means, O king, in olden time were slain by me the great Daitya Tāraka and the valorous Vipracitti.

sanskrit: vātāpir ilvalaś caiva triśirāś ca tathā vibho sundopasundāv asurau kriyayaiva niṣūditau
english: Vātāpi and Ilvala, and Triśiras as well, O lord, and the asuras Sunda and Upasunda—all were destroyed by stratagem alone.

sanskrit: kriyābhyupāyair indreṇa tridivaṃ bhujyate vibho kriyā balavatī rājan nānyat kiṃ cid yudhiṣṭhira
english: By ways and means does Indra enjoy the threefold heaven, O lord. Stratagem is mighty, O king; there is nothing else like it, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: daityāś ca dānavāś caiva rākṣasāḥ pārthivās tathā kriyābhyupāyair nihatāḥ kriyāṃ tasmāt samācara
english: Daityas and Dānavas, rākṣasas and kings alike, have been slain by ways and means; therefore put a stratagem into practice.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca ity ukto vāsudevena pāṇḍavaḥ saṃśitavrataḥ jalasthaṃ taṃ mahārāja tava putraṃ mahābalam abhyabhāṣata kaunteyaḥ prahasann iva bhārata
english: Saṃjaya said: Thus addressed by Vāsudeva, the Pāṇḍava of firm vows, the son of Kuntī, O great king, spoke to your mighty son who stood within the water, smiling as it were, O Bhārata:

sanskrit: suyodhana kimartho 'yam ārambho 'psu kṛtas tvayā sarvaṃ kṣatraṃ ghātayitvā svakulaṃ ca viśāṃ pate
english: "Suyodhana, to what end is this resort to the waters made by you, after you have brought to ruin all the warrior-folk and your own kin as well, O lord of peoples?"

sanskrit: jalāśayaṃ praviṣṭo 'dya vāñchañ jīvitam ātmanaḥ uttiṣṭha rājan yudhyasva sahāsmābhiḥ suyodhana
english: "Today you have entered the water, craving your own life. Rise, O king, and do battle with us, Suyodhana!"

sanskrit: sa ca darpo naraśreṣṭha sa ca mānaḥ kva te gataḥ yas tvaṃ saṃstabhya salilaṃ bhīto rājan vyavasthitaḥ
english: "Where, O best of men, has that pride of yours gone, and where that arrogance—you who, having stilled the water, stand there in fear, O king?"

sanskrit: sarve tvāṃ śūra ity eva janā jalpanti saṃsadi vyarthaṃ tad bhavato manye śauryaṃ salilaśāyinaḥ
english: "All men proclaim you a hero in the assembly; but I deem that valor of yours, who lie hidden in the water, to be in vain."

sanskrit: uttiṣṭha rājan yudhyasva kṣatriyo 'si kulodbhavaḥ kauraveyo viśeṣeṇa kule janma ca saṃsmara
english: "Rise, O king, and fight! You are a warrior, born of noble line, a Kaurava above all—remember your birth in that house."

sanskrit: sa kathaṃ kaurave vaṃśe praśaṃsañ janma cātmanaḥ yuddhād bhītas tatas toyaṃ praviśya pratitiṣṭhasi
english: "How is it that you, vaunting your birth in the Kaurava line, now in terror of battle have entered the water and there take your stand?"

sanskrit: ayuddham avyavasthānaṃ naiṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ anāryajuṣṭam asvargyaṃ raṇe rājan palāyanam
english: "To refuse battle and to abandon one's post—this is not the eternal law. Flight from the field, O king, is the practice of the ignoble and bars the way to heaven."

sanskrit: kathaṃ pāram agatvā hi yuddhe tvaṃ vai jijīviṣuḥ imān nipatitān dṛṣṭvā putrān bhrātṝn pitṝṃs tathā
english: "How, without having reached the far shore of battle, can you wish to live, having seen these fallen—sons and brothers and fathers alike?"

sanskrit: saṃbandhino vayasyāṃś ca mātulān bāndhavāṃs tathā ghātayitvā kathaṃ tāta hrade tiṣṭhasi sāṃpratam
english: "Having brought to death your kinsmen and your comrades, your uncles and your relations, how, my friend, do you now linger in this lake?"

sanskrit: śūramānī na śūras tvaṃ mithyā vadasi bhārata śūro 'ham iti durbuddhe sarvalokasya śṛṇvataḥ
english: "You fancy yourself a hero, but a hero you are not. Falsely you speak, O Bhārata—'I am a hero!'—you fool, in the hearing of all the world."

sanskrit: na hi śūrāḥ palāyante śatrūn dṛṣṭvā kathaṃ cana brūhi vā tvaṃ yayā dhṛtyā śūra tyajasi saṃgaram
english: "For heroes never flee, in any wise, at the sight of foes. Tell us, then, O hero, by what resolve you forsake the fray."
